claim: Chlamydia trachomatis serovar L2 (Ct) is an obligate intracellular bacterium that does not encode FtsZ.
source: Chlamydia trachomatis serovar L2 (Ct), an obligate intracellular bacterium that does not encode FtsZ, divides by a polarized budding process.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations to Stephens, 1998 and Ouellette et al., 2020 in the introduction.

claim: Chlamydia trachomatis divides by a polarized budding process.
source: Chlamydia trachomatis serovar L2 (Ct), an obligate intracellular bacterium that does not encode FtsZ, divides by a polarized budding process.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations to Abdelrahman et al., 2016 and Ouellette et al., 2022 in the introduction.

claim: FtsK is critical for divisome assembly in Ct.
source: In the absence of FtsZ, we show that FtsK, a chromosomal translocase, is critical for divisome assembly in Ct.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that knocking down FtsK prevents divisome assembly (Figure 5).

claim: Chlamydial FtsK forms discrete foci at the septum and at the base of the progenitor mother cell.
source: Chlamydial FtsK forms discrete foci at the septum and at the base of the progenitor mother cell, and our data indicate that FtsK foci at the base of the mother cell mark the location of nascent divisome complexes that form at the site where a daughter cell will emerge in the next round of division.
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1B and 1C.

claim: FtsK foci at the base of the mother cell mark the location of nascent divisome complexes that form at the site where a daughter cell will emerge in the next round of division.
source: Chlamydial FtsK forms discrete foci at the septum and at the base of the progenitor mother cell, and our data indicate that FtsK foci at the base of the mother cell mark the location of nascent divisome complexes that form at the site where a daughter cell will emerge in the next round of division.
evidence: This is supported by data showing FtsK accumulates at the base of secondary buds (Figure 1G).

claim: The divisome in Ct has a hybrid composition, containing elements of the divisome and elongasome from other bacteria.
source: The divisome in Ct has a hybrid composition, containing elements of the divisome and elongasome from other bacteria, and FtsK is recruited to nascent divisomes prior to the other chlamydial divisome proteins assayed, including the PBP2 and PBP3 transpeptidases, and MreB and MreC.
evidence: This is supported by localization data of divisome and elongasome proteins (Figures 1 and 2).

claim: FtsK is recruited to nascent divisomes prior to the other chlamydial divisome proteins assayed, including the PBP2 and PBP3 transpeptidases, and MreB and MreC.
source: The divisome in Ct has a hybrid composition, containing elements of the divisome and elongasome from other bacteria, and FtsK is recruited to nascent divisomes prior to the other chlamydial divisome proteins assayed, including the PBP2 and PBP3 transpeptidases, and MreB and MreC.
evidence: This is supported by quantification of localization profiles showing FtsK has a higher percentage at the base compared to other proteins (Figure 2C).

claim: Knocking down FtsK prevents divisome assembly in Ct and inhibits cell division and septal peptidoglycan synthesis.
source: Knocking down FtsK prevents divisome assembly in Ct and inhibits cell division and septal peptidoglycan synthesis.
evidence: This is supported by CRISPRi knockdown experiments showing aberrant morphology and loss of divisome protein foci (Figures 4 and 5).

claim: MreB does not function like FtsZ and serve as a scaffold for the assembly of the Ct divisome.
source: We further show that MreB does not function like FtsZ and serve as a scaffold for the assembly of the Ct divisome.
evidence: This is supported by data showing that A22 treatment (which inhibits MreB) does not prevent foci formation by FtsK, PBP2, and PBP3 (Figure 3).

claim: MreB is one of the last proteins recruited to the chlamydial divisome.
source: Rather, MreB is one of the last proteins recruited to the chlamydial divisome, and it is necessary for the formation of septal peptidoglycan rings.
evidence: This is supported by quantification showing MreB has a different localization profile than other divisome proteins (Figure 2C).

claim: MreB is necessary for the formation of septal peptidoglycan rings.
source: Rather, MreB is one of the last proteins recruited to the chlamydial divisome, and it is necessary for the formation of septal peptidoglycan rings.
evidence: This is supported by data showing A22 treatment prevents conversion of PG foci into rings (Figure 7E and F).

claim: Most bacteria divide by binary fission, which occurs through the symmetric division of the parental cell into two daughter cells.
source: Most bacteria divide by a highly conserved process termed binary fission, which occurs through the symmetric division of the parental cell into two daughter cells (Harpring and Cox, 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Harpring and Cox, 2023.

claim: Chlamydia trachomatis divides by a polarized cell division process characterized by an asymmetric expansion of the membrane from one pole of a coccoid cell resulting in the formation of a nascent daughter cell.
source: However, Chlamydia trachomatis serovar L2 (Ct), a coccoid, gram-negative, obligate intracellular bacterium divides by a polarized cell division process characterized by an asymmetric expansion of the membrane from one pole of a coccoid cell resulting in the formation of a nascent daughter cell (Abdelrahman et al., 2016; Ouellette et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Abdelrahman et al., 2016 and Ouellette et al., 2022.

claim: Ct undergoes a biphasic developmental cycle during infection.
source: Ct undergoes a biphasic developmental cycle during infection.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Chlamydia biology supported by citation to Abdelrahman and Belland, 2005.

claim: Non-replicating and infectious elementary bodies (EBs) bind to and are internalized by target cells.
source: Non-replicating and infectious elementary bodies (EBs) bind to and are internalized by target cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Chlamydia developmental cycle.

claim: Following internalization, EBs within a membrane vacuole, termed the inclusion, differentiate into replicating reticulate bodies (RBs).
source: Following internalization, EBs within a membrane vacuole, termed the inclusion, differentiate into replicating reticulate bodies (RBs).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Chlamydia developmental cycle.

claim: After replication, RBs undergo secondary differentiation into EBs, which are released from cells to initiate another round of infection.
source: After replication, RBs undergo secondary differentiation into EBs, which are released from cells to initiate another round of infection (Abdelrahman and Belland, 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Chlamydia developmental cycle supported by citation.

claim: Ct has eliminated several gene products essential for cell division in other bacteria, including FtsZ.
source: In evolving to obligate intracellular dependence, Ct has eliminated several gene products essential for cell division in other bacteria, including the central coordinator of divisome formation, FtsZ (Stephens, 1998; Ouellette et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Stephens, 1998 and Ouellette et al., 2020.

claim: FtsZ is a tubulin-like protein that forms filaments that associate to form a ring at the division plane.
source: This tubulin-like protein forms filaments that associate to form a ring at the division plane (Barrows and Goley, 2021), which serves as a scaffold for the assembly of the other components of the bacterial divisome that regulate the processes of septal peptidoglycan (PG) synthesis and chromosomal translocation.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Barrows and Goley, 2021.

claim: FtsZ serves as a scaffold for the assembly of the other components of the bacterial divisome that regulate the processes of septal peptidoglycan (PG) synthesis and chromosomal translocation.
source: This tubulin-like protein forms filaments that associate to form a ring at the division plane (Barrows and Goley, 2021), which serves as a scaffold for the assembly of the other components of the bacterial divisome that regulate the processes of septal peptidoglycan (PG) synthesis and chromosomal translocation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about FtsZ function.

claim: Of the twelve divisome proteins shown to be essential for cell division in E. coli, Ct encodes homologs of FtsK, FtsQLB, FtsW, and PBP3/FtsI.
source: Of the twelve divisome proteins shown to be essential for cell division in the model gammaproteobacterial organism, E. coli, Ct encodes homologs of FtsK, a chromosomal translocase Ouellette et al., 2012; FtsQLB, regulators of septal PG synthesis (Ouellette et al., 2015; Kaur and Lynn, 2022), FtsW, a septal transglycosylase (Putman et al., 2019), and penicillin-binding protein 3 (PBP3/FtsI), a septal transpeptidase (Ouellette et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to Ouellette et al., 2012, Ouellette et al., 2015, Kaur and Lynn, 2022, and Putman et al., 2019.

claim: FtsK is a chromosomal translocase.
source: Of the twelve divisome proteins shown to be essential for cell division in the model gammaproteobacterial organism, E. coli, Ct encodes homologs of FtsK, a chromosomal translocase Ouellette et al., 2012
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ouellette et al., 2012.

claim: FtsQLB are regulators of septal PG synthesis.
source: FtsQLB, regulators of septal PG synthesis (Ouellette et al., 2015; Kaur and Lynn, 2022)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ouellette et al., 2015 and Kaur and Lynn, 2022.

claim: FtsW is a septal transglycosylase.
source: FtsW, a septal transglycosylase (Putman et al., 2019)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Putman et al., 2019.

claim: PBP3/FtsI is a septal transpeptidase.
source: penicillin-binding protein 3 (PBP3/FtsI), a septal transpeptidase (Ouellette et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ouellette et al., 2012.

claim: Rod-shaped bacteria employ the elongasome, which directs sidewall PG synthesis necessary for cell lengthening and the maintenance of cell shape prior to division.
source: In addition to the divisome, rod-shaped bacteria employ another multiprotein complex, the elongasome, which directs sidewall PG synthesis (Liu et al., 2020) necessary for cell lengthening and the maintenance of cell shape prior to division.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Liu et al., 2020.

claim: Ct encodes several elongasome proteins, including MreB, MreC, RodA, RodZ, and PBP2.
source: Although Ct is a coccoid organism, it encodes several elongasome proteins, including MreB, MreC, RodA, RodZ, and penicillin-binding protein 2 (PBP2), a sidewall transpeptidase (Ouellette et al., 2012; Ouellette et al., 2014; Cox et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ouellette et al., 2012, Ouellette et al., 2014, and Cox et al., 2020.

claim: PBP2 is a sidewall transpeptidase.
source: penicillin-binding protein 2 (PBP2), a sidewall transpeptidase (Ouellette et al., 2012; Ouellette et al., 2014; Cox et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ouellette et al., 2012, Ouellette et al., 2014, and Cox et al., 2020.

claim: MreB is essential for cell division in Ct.
source: The actin-like protein MreB is essential for cell division (Ouellette et al., 2012; Abdelrahman et al., 2016) and forms septal rings in Ct (Kemege et al., 2015; Liechti et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ouellette et al., 2012 and Abdelrahman et al., 2016.

claim: MreB forms septal rings in Ct.
source: The actin-like protein MreB is essential for cell division (Ouellette et al., 2012; Abdelrahman et al., 2016) and forms septal rings in Ct (Kemege et al., 2015; Liechti et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kemege et al., 2015, Liechti et al., 2016, and Lee et al., 2020.

claim: It was previously proposed that MreB replaces FtsZ in Ct and serves as a scaffold necessary for the assembly of the chlamydial divisome.
source: These observations led to the proposal that MreB replaces FtsZ in Ct and serves as a scaffold necessary for the assembly of the chlamydial divisome (Lee et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lee et al., 2020.

claim: Chlamydial cell division is dependent upon elements of the divisome and elongasome from other organisms.
source: While inhibitor studies suggest that chlamydial cell division is dependent upon elements of the divisome and elongasome from other organisms (Ouellette et al., 2012; Abdelrahman et al., 2016; Cox et al., 2020), the composition and ordered assembly of the chlamydial divisome and its distribution during polarized budding are undefined.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ouellette et al., 2012, Abdelrahman et al., 2016, and Cox et al., 2020.

claim: The composition and ordered assembly of the chlamydial divisome and its distribution during polarized budding were undefined prior to this study.
source: While inhibitor studies suggest that chlamydial cell division is dependent upon elements of the divisome and elongasome from other organisms (Ouellette et al., 2012; Abdelrahman et al., 2016; Cox et al., 2020), the composition and ordered assembly of the chlamydial divisome and its distribution during polarized budding are undefined.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction to establish the gap in knowledge.

claim: FtsK interacts with elements of both the elongasome and divisome in Ct.
source: We hypothesized that FtsK, a chromosomal translocase, serves a critical function in regulating the division process of Ct, given previous observations demonstrating it interacts with elements of both the elongasome and divisome (Ouellette et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ouellette et al., 2012.

claim: FtsK is the first protein downstream of FtsZ encoded by Ct in the E. coli linear divisome assembly pathway.
source: In the E. coli linear divisome assembly pathway (Du and Lutkenhaus, 2017), FtsK is the first protein downstream of FtsZ encoded by Ct (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Du and Lutkenhaus, 2017 and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: In other organisms, FtsK is uniformly distributed at the septum of dividing cells.
source: In other organisms, FtsK is uniformly distributed at the septum of dividing cells (Yu et al., 1998; Wang et al., 2006; Veiga and Pinho, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Yu et al., 1998, Wang et al., 2006, and Veiga and Pinho, 2017.

claim: Unlike FtsK in other organisms, chlamydial FtsK accumulates in discrete foci in the membrane of coccoid cells.
source: Our results showed that, unlike FtsK in other organisms, chlamydial FtsK accumulates in discrete foci in the membrane of coccoid cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: In cell division intermediates, FtsK localized in foci at the septum, foci at the septum and at the base of the progenitor mother cell, or foci at the base of the progenitor mother cell only.
source: In cell division intermediates, FtsK localized in foci at the septum, foci at the septum and at the base of the progenitor mother cell, or foci at the base of the progenitor mother cell only (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The chlamydial FtsK foci observed during cell division were not uniformly distributed at the septum, rather septal foci of FtsK were restricted to one side of the MOMP-stained septum.
source: The chlamydial FtsK foci observed during cell division were not uniformly distributed at the septum, rather septal foci of FtsK were restricted to one side of the MOMP-stained septum.
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: FtsK foci were often above or below the MOMP-stained septum.
source: In addition, the FtsK foci were often above or below (marked with arrowheads in Figure 1C) the MOMP-stained septum.
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: FtsK-mCherry accumulates in foci in coccoid cells similar to endogenous FtsK.
source: Imaging analyses of Ct in the lysate revealed that like endogenous FtsK, FtsK-mCherry accumulated in foci in coccoid cells (Figure 1D)
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: FtsK-mCherry localizes in foci at the septum, foci at the septum and at the base of the progenitor mother cell, or foci at the base of the progenitor mother cell only in division intermediates.
source: in division intermediates, it localized in foci at the septum, foci at the septum and at the base of the progenitor mother cell, or foci at the base of the progenitor mother cell only (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The foci of FtsK-mCherry, like endogenous FtsK, were often offset relative to the plane defined by MOMP staining at the septum.
source: The foci of FtsK-mCherry, like endogenous FtsK, were often offset relative to the plane defined by MOMP staining at the septum (arrowhead in Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Overexpression of the FtsK-mCherry fusion had no effect on chlamydial developmental cycle progression and the production of infectious EBs.
source: Inclusion forming unit (IFU) assays demonstrated that overexpression of the FtsK-mCherry fusion had no effect on chlamydial developmental cycle progression and the production of infectious EBs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by IFU assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Approximately 20% of dividing cells have a secondary bud.
source: While it is possible that the population of FtsK at the base of the mother cell is a remnant of FtsK from a previous division, ~20% of dividing cells have a secondary bud (Figure 1F)
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: FtsK and FtsK-mCherry accumulate in foci at the base of secondary buds.
source: and FtsK and FtsK-mCherry accumulate in foci at the base of secondary buds (arrowheads in Figure 1G), suggesting that the population of FtsK at the base of the mother cell corresponds to a nascent divisome complex that forms at the site where the daughter cell will arise in the next round of division.
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: PBP2, PBP3, and MreC fusions accumulated in foci in coccoid cells.
source: Imaging analyses revealed that the PBP2, PBP3, and MreC fusions accumulated in foci in coccoid cells (Figure 2A)
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: In cell division intermediates, the PBP2, PBP3, and MreC fusions accumulated in foci at the septum, in foci at the septum and at the base of the progenitor mother cell, or in foci only at the base of the progenitor mother cell.
source: and in cell division intermediates, the fusions accumulated in foci at the septum, in foci at the septum and at the base of the progenitor mother cell, or in foci only at the base of the progenitor mother cell (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: MreB exhibited a similar localization profile to PBP2, PBP3, and MreC.
source: Similar analyses with an MreB_6xHis fusion (Lee et al., 2020) revealed that MreB exhibited a similar localization profile (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: The PBP2, PBP3, MreC and MreB fusions, like FtsK, were restricted to one side and were often slightly above or slightly below the MOMP-stained septum in dividing cells.
source: Each of these fusions, like FtsK, were restricted to one side and were often slightly above or slightly below (marked with arrowheads in Figure 2B) the MOMP-stained septum in dividing cells.
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The aTc induced overexpression of the PBP2, PBP3, and MreC fusions had no effect on the developmental cycle progression of Ct.
source: IFU assays demonstrated that the aTc induced overexpression of the PBP2, PBP3, and MreC fusions had no effect on the developmental cycle progression of Ct (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by IFU assay data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The foci of the PBP2, PBP3, MreC and MreB fusions were detected at the base of secondary buds.
source: Like FtsK, the foci of the PBP2, PBP3, MreC and MreB fusions were also detected at the base of secondary buds (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The distribution profile of FtsK-mCherry accurately reflected the distribution of endogenous FtsK.
source: Quantification of the localization profiles of endogenous FtsK and the various fusion proteins revealed that the distribution profile of FtsK-mCherry accurately reflected the distribution of endogenous FtsK (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: A greater percentage of FtsK was associated with the base of dividing cells suggesting that FtsK associates with nascent divisomes at the base of dividing cells prior to the other putative divisome proteins assayed.
source: Furthermore, a greater percentage of FtsK was associated with the base of dividing cells (including cells with septum and base, and cells with base alone) suggesting that FtsK associates with nascent divisomes at the base of dividing cells prior to the other putative divisome proteins assayed.
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: MreB associated with nascent divisomes at the base of dividing cells after mCherry-PBP2 and mCherry-PBP3.
source: Finally, this analysis suggested that MreB associated with nascent divisomes at the base of dividing cells after mCherry-PBP2 and mCherry-PBP3 (marked with # in Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The localization profiles of the chlamydial divisome proteins likely reflect the assembly of divisome complexes at the septum and at the base of the progenitor mother cell, and the disassembly of the septal divisome when divisome proteins are only present at the base of the mother cell.
source: The localization profiles of the chlamydial divisome proteins (Figures 1 and 2) likely reflect the assembly of divisome complexes at the septum and at the base of the progenitor mother cell, and the disassembly of the septal divisome when divisome proteins are only present at the base of the mother cell.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the localization data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: FtsK was present in foci at the septum and in foci at the base in dividing cells, while each of the PBP2, PBP3, MreC, and MreB fusions was only detected at the septum where they overlapped the distribution of septal FtsK.
source: Imaging analyses revealed that FtsK was present in foci at the septum and in foci at the base in these cells, while each of the fusions was only detected at the septum where they overlapped the distribution of septal FtsK (Bars are1 μm).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: A22 inhibits chlamydial budding and most cells in the population were coccoid following A22 treatment.
source: As previously shown (Ouellette et al., 2012; Cox et al., 2020), A22 inhibits chlamydial budding and most cells in the population were coccoid following A22 treatment (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ouellette et al., 2012 and Cox et al., 2020, and data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Approximately 50% of the untreated control cells were coccoid, which is consistent with prior estimates of the number of non-dividing RBs at this stage of the developmental cycle.
source: Furthermore, approximately 50% of the untreated control cells were coccoid, which is consistent with prior estimates of the number of non-dividing RBs at this stage of the developmental cycle (Lee et al., 2018), indicating that our lysis procedure does not lead to a bias in the number of non-dividing coccoid cells in the population.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lee et al., 2018 and data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: MreB in coccoid cells adopted a diffuse pattern of localization following A22 treatment.
source: MreB in coccoid cells adopted a diffuse pattern of localization following A22 treatment (Figure 3).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3.

claim: A22 had a statistically significant effect on the percent of coccoid cells containing MreC foci.
source: A22 also had a statistically significant effect on the percent of coccoid cells containing MreC foci, but it did not affect the ability of FtsK, PBP2, or PBP3 to form foci in coccoid cells (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: A22 did not affect the ability of FtsK, PBP2, or PBP3 to form foci in coccoid cells.
source: A22 also had a statistically significant effect on the percent of coccoid cells containing MreC foci, but it did not affect the ability of FtsK, PBP2, or PBP3 to form foci in coccoid cells (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: MreB filaments do not function as a scaffold that is necessary for the assembly of all divisome components in Ct.
source: These data indicate that MreB filaments do not function as a scaffold that is necessary for the assembly of all divisome components in Ct.
evidence: This is inferred from the A22 treatment data showing FtsK, PBP2, and PBP3 can form foci without MreB filaments.

claim: The induction of dCas12 resulted in ~10 fold reduction in ftsK transcript levels by 15 hpi in cells expressing the ftsK-targeting crRNA.
source: This analysis revealed that the induction of dCas12 resulted in ~10 fold reduction in ftsK transcript levels by 15 hpi in cells expressing the ftsK-targeting crRNA (Figure 4A)
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The induction of dCas12 resulted in ~ eightfold reduction in pbp2 transcript levels in cells expressing the pbp2-targeting crRNA.
source: and ~ eightfold reduction in pbp2 transcript levels in cells expressing the pbp2-targeting crRNA (Figure 4B)
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The ftsK and pbp2 crRNAs had minimal or no effect on chlamydial euo and omcB transcript levels.
source: while these crRNAs had minimal or no effect on chlamydial euo and omcB transcript levels, suggesting that the ftsK and pbp2 crRNAs specifically inhibit the transcription of ftsK and pbp2 (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: Ct morphology was normal and dCas12 was undetectable in the inclusions of uninduced control cells.
source: Imaging analysis revealed that Ct morphology was normal and dCas12 was undetectable in the inclusions of uninduced control cells, while foci of dCas12 were observed in the induced cells, and Ct in the inclusion exhibited an enlarged aberrant morphology (Figure 4C and D)
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: Foci of dCas12 were observed in the induced cells, and Ct in the inclusion exhibited an enlarged aberrant morphology.
source: Imaging analysis revealed that Ct morphology was normal and dCas12 was undetectable in the inclusions of uninduced control cells, while foci of dCas12 were observed in the induced cells, and Ct in the inclusion exhibited an enlarged aberrant morphology (Figure 4C and D), suggesting that the inducible knockdown of ftsK or pbp2 blocks chlamydial cell division.
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: The inducible knockdown of ftsK or pbp2 blocks chlamydial cell division.
source: Imaging analysis revealed that Ct morphology was normal and dCas12 was undetectable in the inclusions of uninduced control cells, while foci of dCas12 were observed in the induced cells, and Ct in the inclusion exhibited an enlarged aberrant morphology (Figure 4C and D), suggesting that the inducible knockdown of ftsK or pbp2 blocks chlamydial cell division.
evidence: This is inferred from the aberrant morphology observed in knockdown cells.

claim: Foci of endogenous FtsK and PBP2 were almost undetectable when ftsK or pbp2 were transiently knocked down using CRISPRi.
source: In additional studies, we induced dCas12 at 17 hpi in cells expressing the ftsK or pbp2-targeting crRNAs. Lysates were prepared and the cells were fixed at 21 hpi, and localization studies revealed that foci of endogenous FtsK and PBP2 were almost undetectable when ftsK or pbp2 were transiently knocked down using this CRISPRi approach (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Greater than 60% of the Ct in the uninduced controls were at various stages of polarized budding.
source: These analyses revealed that >60% of the Ct in the uninduced controls were at various stages of polarized budding (Figure 5A and B)
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: Approximately 90% of the cells were coccoid when ftsK was knocked down.
source: while ~90% of the cells were coccoid when ftsK was knocked down (Figure 5A)
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Approximately 85% of the cells were coccoid following pbp2 knockdown.
source: and ~85% of the cells were coccoid following pbp2 knockdown (Figure 5B), suggesting that the initiation of polarized budding of Ct is inhibited when ftsK or pbp2 are knocked down.
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The initiation of polarized budding of Ct is inhibited when ftsK or pbp2 are knocked down.
source: and ~85% of the cells were coccoid following pbp2 knockdown (Figure 5B), suggesting that the initiation of polarized budding of Ct is inhibited when ftsK or pbp2 are knocked down.
evidence: This is inferred from the increase in coccoid cells following knockdown.

claim: The number of coccoid cells with polarized foci of PBP2 and PBP3 were reduced by approximately 80% following ftsK knockdown.
source: This analysis revealed that the number of coccoid cells with polarized foci of PBP2 and PBP3 were reduced by approximately 80% following ftsK knockdown (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: FtsK retained its ability to form foci in coccoid cells following pbp2 knockdown.
source: While FtsK retained its ability to form foci in coccoid cells following pbp2 knockdown, foci of PBP3 were almost entirely absent in pbp2 knockdown cells (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: Foci of PBP3 were almost entirely absent in pbp2 knockdown cells.
source: While FtsK retained its ability to form foci in coccoid cells following pbp2 knockdown, foci of PBP3 were almost entirely absent in pbp2 knockdown cells (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: FtsK is necessary for foci formation by both the PBP2 and PBP3 transpeptidases.
source: Quantification of these assays revealed that FtsK is necessary for foci formation by both the PBP2 and PBP3 transpeptidases, while PBP2 is necessary for foci formation by PBP3 (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5E and F.

claim: PBP2 is necessary for foci formation by PBP3.
source: Quantification of these assays revealed that FtsK is necessary for foci formation by both the PBP2 and PBP3 transpeptidases, while PBP2 is necessary for foci formation by PBP3 (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5E and F.

claim: FtsK is upstream of, and necessary for, the addition of PBP2 and PBP3 to the Ct divisome.
source: Our data place FtsK upstream of, and necessary for, the addition of PBP2 and PBP3 to the Ct divisome, and PBP2 upstream of and necessary for the addition of PBP3 to the Ct divisome.
evidence: This is inferred from the knockdown experiments showing FtsK is required for PBP2 and PBP3 foci formation.

claim: PBP2 is upstream of and necessary for the addition of PBP3 to the Ct divisome.
source: Our data place FtsK upstream of, and necessary for, the addition of PBP2 and PBP3 to the Ct divisome, and PBP2 upstream of and necessary for the addition of PBP3 to the Ct divisome.
evidence: This is inferred from the knockdown experiments showing PBP2 is required for PBP3 foci formation.

claim: The results are consistent with inhibitor studies that indicated PBP2 acts upstream of PBP3 in the polarized budding process of Ct.
source: These results are consistent with inhibitor studies that indicated PBP2 acts upstream of PBP3 in the polarized budding process of Ct (Cox et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Cox et al., 2020.

claim: Mecillinam is an inhibitor of the transpeptidase activity of PBP2.
source: To investigate whether the catalytic activity of PBP2 is necessary to maintain its association with the Ct divisome, HeLa cells were infected with Ct, and mecillinam, an inhibitor of the transpeptidase activity of PBP2 (Kocaoglu et al., 2015; Cox et al., 2020), was added to the media of infected cells at 20 hpi.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kocaoglu et al., 2015 and Cox et al., 2020.

claim: Mecillinam blocks chlamydial division.
source: As shown previously, mecillinam blocks chlamydial division (Ouellette et al., 2012; Cox et al., 2020), and most cells in the population assumed a coccoid morphology (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ouellette et al., 2012 and Cox et al., 2020, and data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Mecillinam treatment resulted in a ~50% reduction in the number of cells with polarized foci of PBP2.
source: Mecillinam treatment resulted in a ~50% reduction in the number of cells with polarized foci of PBP2 (Figure 6B-E).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6B-E.

claim: There was a similar reduction in polarized foci of PBP3 following mecillinam treatment.
source: There was a similar reduction in polarized foci of PBP3 following mecillinam treatment (Figure 6B-E).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6B-E.

claim: The catalytic activity of PBP2 is necessary for PBP2 to efficiently associate with or maintain its association with polarized divisome complexes.
source: These data indicate that the catalytic activity of PBP2 is necessary for PBP2 to efficiently associate with or maintain its association with polarized divisome complexes.
evidence: This is inferred from the mecillinam treatment data showing reduced PBP2 foci.

claim: PBP3 association with the divisome complex is dependent on the prior addition of PBP2 to the complex.
source: Furthermore, consistent with pbp2 knockdown studies, PBP3 association with the divisome complex is dependent on the prior addition of PBP2 to the complex, but foci formation by FtsK is unaffected when PBP2 foci are reduced in number (Figure 6).
evidence: This is inferred from the mecillinam treatment data showing reduced PBP3 foci when PBP2 is inhibited.

claim: Foci formation by FtsK is unaffected when PBP2 foci are reduced in number.
source: Furthermore, consistent with pbp2 knockdown studies, PBP3 association with the divisome complex is dependent on the prior addition of PBP2 to the complex, but foci formation by FtsK is unaffected when PBP2 foci are reduced in number (Figure 6).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6.

claim: PG foci, bars, and rings were detected in dividing Ct using EDA-DA labeling.
source: This approach enabled the detection of PG foci, bars, and rings in dividing Ct (Liechti, 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Liechti, 2021 and imaging data in Figure 7.

claim: In some instances PG foci were detected at both the septum and at the base of the progenitor mother cell.
source: Our imaging analysis revealed that in some instances PG foci were detected at both the septum and at the base of the progenitor mother cell (Figure 7A)
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: In other instances, PG organization at the septum and the base differed.
source: and in other instances, PG organization at the septum and the base differed. In the example shown (Figure 7B), a PG foci was detected at the septum while a PG ring was detected at the base of the mother cell.
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Multiple foci of PBP3 were associated with a septal PG ring.
source: This analysis, which was restricted to PG formation at the septum of dividing cells, revealed that multiple foci of PBP3 were associated with a septal PG ring (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The PG ring was at an angle relative to the MOMP-stained septum.
source: Furthermore, the PG ring was at an angle relative to the MOMP-stained septum.
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Two foci of endogenous FtsK were associated with PG that was at an angle relative to the MOMP-stained septum.
source: Similar analyses revealed that two foci of endogenous FtsK were associated with PG that was again at an angle relative to the MOMP-stained septum. This was true even though the PG had not fully reorganized into a ring structure (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Foci, bars, or rings were detected in ~80% of untreated coccoid cells.
source: We detected foci, bars, or rings in ~80% of untreated coccoid cells (Figure 7D and E), which make up ~50% of the cells in the inclusion at this stage of the developmental cycle (Lee et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 7D and E.

claim: Each of the PG intermediates (foci, bars, rings) exhibited a polarized distribution in untreated coccoid cells.
source: Furthermore, each of these PG intermediates exhibited a polarized distribution in untreated coccoid cells (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: PG rings can arise prior to any of the morphological changes that occur during the polarized division of Ct.
source: Although we cannot rule out that continued PG synthesis and reorganization occurs in polarized division intermediates, PG rings can arise prior to any of the morphological changes that occur during the polarized division of Ct.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of PG rings in coccoid cells.

claim: Inhibitors of MreB filament formation prevent the appearance of PG-containing structures in Ct.
source: Prior studies have shown that inhibitors of MreB filament formation prevent the appearance of PG-containing structures in Ct (Liechti et al., 2014; Ouellette et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Liechti et al., 2014 and Ouellette et al., 2022.

claim: PG was diffuse/undetectable in the majority of A22-treated cells.
source: These analyses revealed that PG was diffuse/undetectable in the majority of A22-treated cells, and, in those cells where PG was still detected, it could not convert into ring structures (Figure 7E and F).
evidence: This is supported by quantification and imaging data shown in Figure 7E and F.

claim: In A22-treated cells where PG was still detected, it could not convert into ring structures.
source: These analyses revealed that PG was diffuse/undetectable in the majority of A22-treated cells, and, in those cells where PG was still detected, it could not convert into ring structures (Figure 7E and F).
evidence: This is supported by quantification and imaging data shown in Figure 7E and F.

claim: PG formed discrete foci or bars in 60% of mecillinam-treated cells.
source: In similar experiments, we assessed the effect of mecillinam on the appearance of PG intermediates in coccoid cells. These analyses revealed that PG formed discrete foci or bars in 60% of mecillinam-treated cells (Figure 7E and F).
evidence: This is supported by quantification and imaging data shown in Figure 7E and F.

claim: PG intermediates could not convert into PG rings when the transpeptidase activity of PBP2 was inhibited.
source: However, these PG intermediates could not convert into PG rings when the transpeptidase activity of PBP2 was inhibited.
evidence: This is supported by quantification and imaging data shown in Figure 7E and F.

claim: PG localization was diffuse/undetectable in ~90% of the cells assayed following ftsK knockdown.
source: Finally, we assessed PG organization in cells where ftsK was knocked down by inducing dCas12 in the ftsK knockdown strain by the addition of aTc to the media of infected cells at 17 hpi. Cells were fixed at 21 hpi, and localization studies revealed that ftsK knockdown had the most dramatic effect on PG localization, which was diffuse/undetectable in ~90% of the cells assayed.
evidence: This is supported by quantification and imaging data shown in Figure 7E and F.

claim: Inhibiting divisome assembly by knocking down ftsK almost entirely prevented the accumulation of all PG-containing intermediates in Ct.
source: Inhibiting divisome assembly by knocking down ftsK almost entirely prevented the accumulation of all PG-containing intermediates in Ct (Figure 7E and F).
evidence: This is supported by quantification and imaging data shown in Figure 7E and F.

claim: This study is the first to document the ordered assembly of divisome proteins in Ct.
source: This study is the first to document the ordered assembly of divisome proteins in Ct and to investigate the roles of divisome proteins in regulating PG synthesis/organization in this obligate intracellular bacterial pathogen.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: This study is the first to investigate the roles of divisome proteins in regulating PG synthesis/organization in Ct.
source: This study is the first to document the ordered assembly of divisome proteins in Ct and to investigate the roles of divisome proteins in regulating PG synthesis/organization in this obligate intracellular bacterial pathogen.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: The domain organization of FtsK is highly conserved among bacteria.
source: The domain organization of FtsK is highly conserved among bacteria.
evidence: This is established knowledge about FtsK.

claim: The C-terminus of FtsK mediates the ATP-dependent directional translocation of the protein along DNA through interaction with KOPS.
source: The C-terminus of the protein mediates the ATP-dependent directional translocation of the protein along DNA through interaction with KOPS (FtsK orienting polar sequences) (Barre et al., 2001; Massey et al., 2006)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Barre et al., 2001 and Massey et al., 2006.

claim: The C-terminus of FtsK stimulates XerCD-dependent recombination at the dif site near the chromosomal terminus to decatenate chromosomal dimers that arise from homologous recombination during DNA replication to monomers.
source: and stimulates XerCD-dependent recombination at the dif site near the chromosomal terminus to decatenate chromosomal dimers that arise from homologous recombination during DNA replication to monomers (Blakely et al., 1993; Massey et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Blakely et al., 1993 and Massey et al., 2006.

claim: The C-terminus of chlamydial FtsK is 41% identical to the C-terminus of E. coli FtsK.
source: The C-terminus of chlamydial FtsK is 41% identical to the C-terminus of E. coli FtsK.
evidence: This is a sequence comparison result.

claim: The N-terminus of E. coli FtsK encodes four predicted transmembrane spanning helices, which are sufficient to direct the protein to the septum in dividing cells.
source: The N-terminus of E. coli FtsK encodes four predicted transmembrane spanning helices, which are sufficient to direct the protein to the septum in dividing cells (Yu et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yu et al., 1998.

claim: The N-terminus of chlamydial FtsK is predicted to encode four transmembrane-spanning helices.
source: The N-terminus of chlamydial FtsK, which is also predicted to encode four transmembrane-spanning helices, is 34% identical to E. coli FtsK.
evidence: This is a prediction based on sequence analysis.

claim: The N-terminus of chlamydial FtsK is 34% identical to E. coli FtsK.
source: The N-terminus of chlamydial FtsK, which is also predicted to encode four transmembrane-spanning helices, is 34% identical to E. coli FtsK.
evidence: This is a sequence comparison result.

claim: There was no correlation between the stage of bud formation by the initial bud and the appearance of nascent divisomes at the base of the progenitor mother cell.
source: Our analyses further revealed there was no correlation between the stage of bud formation by the initial bud (early, mid-late; Ouellette et al., 2022), and the appearance of nascent divisomes at the base of the progenitor mother cell (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: MreB and MreC can reorganize into rings in dividing cells.
source: The lack of overlap of FtsK with MreB and MreC is most clearly evident in Figure 2—figure supplement 4A, and while it is unclear why FtsK only partially overlaps the distribution of the other divisome components in dividing Ct, MreB (Liechti et al., 2014; Kemege et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2020) and MreC (Figure 2—figure supplement 5A) can reorganize into rings in dividing cells
evidence: This is supported by citations to Liechti et al., 2014, Kemege et al., 2015, Lee et al., 2020, and imaging data in Figure 2—figure supplement 5A.

claim: MreC rings were at an angle relative to the MOMP-stained septum.
source: and the MreC rings we detected, like PG rings (Figure 7), were at an angle relative to the MOMP-stained septum.
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5A and Figure 7.

claim: MreC forms rings in coccoid cells.
source: MreC also forms rings in coccoid cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 5B).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5B.

claim: FtsK rings were never detected in dividing or coccoid chlamydial cells.
source: Although MreB and MreC form rings in Ct, we never detected FtsK rings in dividing or coccoid chlamydial cells.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on imaging observations.

claim: The angled orientation of PG and MreC rings relative to the MOMP-stained septum in division intermediates appears to be a conserved feature of the cell division process.
source: The relevance of the angled orientation of PG and MreC rings relative to the MOMP-stained septum in division intermediates is unclear. However, it appears to be a conserved feature of the cell division process and may arise because the divisome proteins are often positioned slightly above or below the plane of the MOMP-stained septum (Figures 1 and 2).
evidence: This is inferred from the consistent observation of angled rings in the imaging data.

claim: The angled orientation may arise because the divisome proteins are often positioned slightly above or below the plane of the MOMP-stained septum.
source: The relevance of the angled orientation of PG and MreC rings relative to the MOMP-stained septum in division intermediates is unclear. However, it appears to be a conserved feature of the cell division process and may arise because the divisome proteins are often positioned slightly above or below the plane of the MOMP-stained septum (Figures 1 and 2).
evidence: This is speculated based on the imaging observations.

claim: MreB filaments are necessary for the conversion of PG foci into PG rings in Ct.
source: Although our data indicate that MreB filaments do not form a scaffold necessary for the assembly of all components of the divisome in Ct, MreB filaments are necessary for the conversion of PG foci into PG rings in Ct (Figure 7).
evidence: This is supported by data showing A22 treatment prevents PG ring formation (Figure 7).

claim: FtsZ treadmilling drives its rotational movement at the septum and this may be required for the positioning of peptidoglycan biosynthetic enzymes at the division plane in gram-negative and gram-positive bacteria.
source: FtsZ treadmilling drives its rotational movement at the septum and this may be required for the positioning of peptidoglycan biosynthetic enzymes at the division plane in gram-negative and gram-positive bacteria (Bisson-Filho et al., 2017; Yang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bisson-Filho et al., 2017 and Yang et al., 2017.

claim: In the absence of FtsZ, chlamydial FtsK is critical for divisome assembly and PG synthesis in Ct.
source: The knockdown studies presented here demonstrated that in the absence of FtsZ, chlamydial FtsK is critical for divisome assembly and PG synthesis in Ct
evidence: This is supported by the knockdown experiments shown in Figures 4, 5, and 7.

claim: Ct is a member of the Planctomycetes/Verrucomicrobia/Chlamydia superphylum.
source: Ct is a member of the Planctomycetes/Verrucomicrobia/Chlamydia superphylum and members of the Chlamydia and Planctomycetes phyla do not encode FtsZ (Rivas-Marín et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Rivas-Marín et al., 2016.

claim: Members of the Chlamydia and Planctomycetes phyla do not encode FtsZ.
source: Ct is a member of the Planctomycetes/Verrucomicrobia/Chlamydia superphylum and members of the Chlamydia and Planctomycetes phyla do not encode FtsZ (Rivas-Marín et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Rivas-Marín et al., 2016.

claim: Planctospirus limnophila is a member of the Planctomycetes that divides by polarized budding.
source: Planctospirus limnophila is a member of the Planctomycetes that divides by polarized budding, and recent knockout studies (Rivas-Marin et al., 2023) indicated that FtsK is the only protein of the chlamydial divisome we characterized here that is essential for the growth of this free-living organism.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Rivas-Marin et al., 2023.

claim: FtsK is the only protein of the chlamydial divisome characterized in this study that is essential for the growth of Planctospirus limnophila.
source: Planctospirus limnophila is a member of the Planctomycetes that divides by polarized budding, and recent knockout studies (Rivas-Marin et al., 2023) indicated that FtsK is the only protein of the chlamydial divisome we characterized here that is essential for the growth of this free-living organism.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Rivas-Marin et al., 2023.

claim: Multiple mechanisms of FtsZ-independent polarized budding have evolved in members of the Planctomycetes/Verrucomicrobia/Chlamydia superphyla.
source: These results suggest that multiple mechanisms of FtsZ-independent polarized budding have evolved in members of this superphyla.
evidence: This is inferred from the differences in essential divisome proteins between Ct and Planctospirus limnophila.
